messages.subject: Measurement invariance
parts:
Hi,

I'm having some trouble implementing the Lavaan measurement invariance procedure (I followed the 2017 Lavaan Tutorial). I want to see whether a 7 factor model is invariant across gender. My syntax is below. Any help would be greatly appreciated! :

library(semTools)

Sample <- read.dta("c:/Users/Laptop/Desktop/Statafile.dta ")

 

library(lavaan)

model5 <- '

  # measurement model

Belonging =~ SAFit + SAGeA + SAAcM

Stigma =~ SASel + SAPun + SADam + SAUnwa

SelfPunishment =~ SADeSu + SAWor + SADeSc

CoerciveHelp =~ SAHel + SASho + SAMak

Escape =~ SACle + SASto + SATe + SACha

Dependence =~ SAOnM + SAOnO + SALiB + SALiW + SAOnT

Revenge =~ SAGeB + SAShP + SAInt + SaFoR

   '

 

summary(fit5, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures = TRUE)

measurementInvariance(model5, data = Sample, group = "Gender3")

messages.subject: Re: Measurement invariance
parts: Thanks for your reply; I dont understand why measurement invariance is included in the July 16, 2017 Lavaan tutorial if that's the case. And see the attached too.

I'm not sure which tutorial you are referring to, but the one on the website states the same information:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

And notice in the slides you posted, semTools is called on slide 72.  So that should allow you to use that function.
So I should be using the lavaan library and things like the following, rather than running the defunct "measurementInvariance()" function?:

It is not defunct.  Yves wrote it as part of the lavaan package before there was a semTools package.  In 2012 it was decided to start a package with a bunch of miscellaneous tools that extended the functionality of lavaan, so after semTools was born Yves simply passed the maintenance of the measurementInvariance() function over to the semTools maintainers.   You can use multiple R packages in tandem.  There are many packages that build on core packages.  lavaan itself is the center of a large ecosystem on CRAN, include lavaan.survey, simsem, semTools, onyx, semPlot, and blavaan.

So you can use measurementInvariance(), just load the semTools package to access it.  Or you can fit your models manually, which will be more useful (maybe even necessary) whenever you have special issues that do not fit into the simple default template described in the slides.
